newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan panel cites lack of manager for nuclear woes.
newsitem.headline: Japan panel cites lack of manager for nuclear woes.

text.p: A panel studying reforms of Japan's troubled state-run nuclear power firm on Friday blamed a series of accidents at the firm's facilities on the absence of an authoritative manager.

Hiroyuki Yoshikawa, the former president of Tokyo University, said in the report published on Friday that the accidents could be attributed to "an absence of...a manager charged with authority and responsibility over the organisation."

The panel chaired by Yoshikawa is looking into troubles at the Power Reactor and Nuclear Fuel Development Corp (PNC), which operates the Tokaimura nuclear fuel reprocessing plant, site of a fire and explosion which exposed 37 workers to low-level radiation in March.
The PNC also operates the prototype fast-breeder reactor "Monju" on the Sea of Japan coast, which has been shut since an accident in December 1995 involving a coolant leak.
The fate of the PNC, particularly the reprocessing plant and Monju, has been a central theme in an ongoing debate over nuclear power policy in resource-poor Japan.

Earlier on Friday an official with the Science and Technology Agency, which supervises nuclear power technology, denied a newspaper report that it had decided to scrap the Tokaimura reprocessing plant.
The panel is due to come up with a report on recommended reforms of the PNC which will be presented to the government, which will make a final decision on the future of the PNC.
The final government decision is due around July or August, government officials said.
They said that August was the deadline for a fiscal budget request, and that this deadline would have to be met if the fate of the PNC required budget spending.
